action_history.rationale: Model: Sum of 7 pseudo-Voigt peaks on a linear baseline (Levenberg-Marquardt least squares); reseeded/retuned peak_1 (~141) and peak_4 (~394) to narrower FWHM + intermediate-high eta, reassigned peak_2 (~197 narrow) and peak_3 (~307 broad hump), FWHM capped at 50 cm-1; flat/linear baseline confirmed (rolling-min baseline area fraction = 0.206, not fluorescence-dominated)

result.detailed_analysis: The fitted band positions are 141.1, 196.6, 297.0, 393.6, 514.4, 636.4, and 794.3 cm-1. The four best-constrained bands (141.1 +/- 0.03, 393.6 +/- 0.06, 514.4 +/- 0.08, 636.4 +/- 0.47) match the canonical Raman-active modes of anatase TiO2: Eg ~144 (very strong), B1g ~399, A1g/B1g ~516, and Eg ~639 cm-1. The weak fitted band at ~197 corresponds well to the weak anatase Eg mode near 197 cm-1 (often near detection limit), reinforcing the assignment. The dominant ~141 band being ~10-20x stronger than the others and its Lorentzian character (eta ~1) are both textbook anatase behavior. The measured position of 141.1 cm-1 (slightly below the ideal 144) is consistent with anatase; small downshifts/broadening can arise from larger crystallite sizes or the fit's symmetric-profile limitation. Peaks 3 (~297, broad, FWHM pinned at 50) and 7 (~794, broad) are weakly constrained and likely represent either background curvature, a minor second-order feature, or genuine weak modes that the symmetric model cannot cleanly resolve; they should not be treated as diagnostic. Notably there is NO strong band near 447/612 cm-1 (rutile) and none near 235, so a rutile-dominated assignment is excluded; the pattern is specifically anatase. R2 = 0.987 with a flat baseline confirms a good overall description, but the persistent M-shaped residual on the main band (~+/-30000 counts locally) means peak-shape-derived quantities (exact FWHM, crystallite-size inferences) carry systematic error. Compact band summary (center cm-1, relative intensity, strongest first): 141.1 (1.00), 393.6 (0.60), 514.4 (0.44), 636.4 (0.075), 794.3 (0.019), 297.0 (0.014), 196.6 (0.012).

scientific_claims.claim: The Raman spectrum is identified as anatase TiO2, with its dominant Eg mode at 141.1 +/- 0.03 cm-1 and characteristic companion bands at 393.6 +/- 0.06 (B1g), 514.4 +/- 0.08 (A1g/B1g), and 636.4 +/- 0.47 cm-1 (Eg).
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: The full band pattern (positions and the strong intensity hierarchy dominated by the ~141 cm-1 mode) uniquely fingerprints anatase over rutile or brookite polymorphs, enabling phase identification of the unknown compound; the tightly constrained low-frequency Eg position is a sensitive probe of crystallite size and strain.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone observed anatase TiO2 with its Eg mode systematically downshifted to ~141 cm-1, and what crystallite-size or strain conditions produce this shift?

result.model_type: Sum of 7 pseudo-Voigt peaks on a linear baseline (Levenberg-Marquardt least squares); reseeded/retuned peak_1 (~141) and peak_4 (~394) to narrower FWHM + intermediate-high eta, reassigned peak_2 (~197 narrow) and peak_3 (~307 broad hump), FWHM capped at 50 cm-1; flat/linear baseline confirmed (rolling-min baseline area fraction = 0.206, not fluorescence-dominated)

verification_iterations.model: Sum of 7 pseudo-Voigt peaks on a linear baseline. Each peak: A·[η·Lorentzian(x;x0,Γ) + (1−η)·Gaussian(x;x0,Γ)], with independent amplitude A, center x0, width Γ, and mixing η per band. Band centers (initial): ~140, ~195, ~300, ~395, ~515, ~637, ~790 cm⁻¹. Baseline: y = m·x + b (expected near zero slope).

issues.problem: The dominant peak is poorly modeled by a single pure-Lorentzian (eta≈1.0) pseudo-Voigt. The data rises more steeply and is sharper/narrower at the top than the fit, leaving a strong M-shaped residual (±30000 counts, ~987σ).
Systematic oscillatory residual on the rising edge and top of the 394 peak — the fit lags the leading edge and misses the sharp apex.
The fit fails to capture a real, broad low-intensity feature/shoulder centered near x≈300–310 that sits well above baseline in the data.

These components are broad, low-amplitude, high-uncertainty terms with near-zero eta and giant FWHM (35, 105, 148) that do not track the real narrow data features in their regions and produce the strongly negative red fit excursions between the main peaks (e.g. the fit dips to -1000 near x≈240 where data is flat/positive).

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Reseed and retune within the locked 7-peak model: sharpen/adjust peak_1 (eta, fwhm) to fix the M-shaped core residual, retune peak_4 shape on its leading edge, and move a weak component (peak_2/peak_3) to seed the real hump at x≈305 rather than leaving them fitting valleys with unphysical eta≈0.

verification_iterations.model: Sum of 7 pseudo-Voigt peaks on a linear baseline (y = m·x + b, expected near-zero slope). Each peak: A·[η·Lorentzian(x;x0,Γ) + (1−η)·Gaussian(x;x0,Γ)] with independent amplitude A, center x0, width Γ, and mixing η. Band assignments refined from verification feedback: peak_1 (~141) is a sharp, strong band whose core requires a narrower Γ and intermediate-to-high η so the pseudo-Voigt reproduces both the sharp apex and the wings without an M-shaped residual; peak_4 (~394) is a strong band needing a narrower Γ and retuned η to track its steep leading edge and sharp apex; peaks 2 and 3 are reassigned away from valley-fitting roles — one is reseeded to the real narrow feature near ~195–200 and the other to the real broad low-intensity hump near ~305–310 (~2500 counts); peaks 5 (~515), 6 (~637), and 7 (~790) retain their original band roles, with peak_7 width constrained to a physical range so it stops producing negative excursions. All within the locked 7-pseudo-Voigt + linear-baseline model.

issues.problem: The dominant peak retains an M-shaped residual: the pure-Lorentzian (eta≈1.0) tails run wide while the apex is slightly under-shot, so the data is sharper/narrower near the top than the fit.
Mild oscillatory residual on the rising edge and apex of the 394 peak.
